description:
FightGuy's air.3, Flip Kick: his up aerial. In the air he does one full backflip, and his straight right leg sweeps with it from in front of him, up over his head, to behind him, like a shoto's flash kick done in mid air. The foot is the hitbox, so its path is the move: anyone in front of him, above him or close behind him gets kicked.

Who he is. FightGuy is a classic shoto and a genuinely talented martial artist, the underground champion, proud of it, a bit dumb and very full of himself (image 1): smug grin, big chin, spiky black mullet, red headband, blue sleeveless gi top, white baggy gi pants, red belt and hand wraps, barefoot. His moves are clean, snappy martial arts with a show-off edge, readable from behind: big clear silhouettes, a crisp kick with a straight leg and a pointed foot.

How the game plays it. The match camera sits straight behind him, so the action must read from behind: the leg goes up through the middle, over his head, and the flip turns his body toward the camera. The game plays this 96-tick clip at about double speed. The fighter does not travel in the clip; the game moves him. Only the hips joint may translate, so turn the body about its middle (around the belly), not about the hips joint, so he flips in place. The game crossfades in and out over about 0.1 s.

In the air. Tick 0 and tick 96 are his fall pose exactly (image 1). There is no floor contact.

The flip. The whole body pitches backward (head going back and down, feet going forward and up) one full turn, 360 degrees, about his right-left axis. The right leg stays straight from the hip to the pointed toes through the kick, held out in front of his body at about 80-100 degrees from the spine, so as the body pitches back the foot travels front, then straight up, then behind: an L shape turning over. The left leg tucks, knee to chest, through the kick. The kick's path stays on his centre line: the right foot is never more than a few centimetres to the right of the middle of his body, not out beside his hip.

The move (96 ticks, played once):
- Tick 0: the fall pose.
- Tick 12, the load: he gathers, both knees come up a little, chin tucks, the chest curls forward over the knees and the arms swing down and back past the hips; the body has not started turning yet.
- Tick 20, the kick starts in front: he snaps the straight right leg forward and up, foot pointed, about hip height and well ahead of his hips; his upper body leans back about 20-30 degrees to throw it; the left knee tucks to the chest; arms go out wide to his sides.
- Tick 32, the foot is straight above him: his body has pitched back about 90 degrees, lying on his back in the air with his head behind him and his chest facing up, and the straight right leg points straight up with the foot above his head height and above his hips on the centre line; the left knee stays tucked; arms out wide to both sides, palms open, for balance.
- Tick 44, the foot is behind him: the body is nearly upside down (about 170 degrees), head down below his hips, the straight right leg now pointing back behind him (the opposite side from where he faces).
- Tick 58, the tuck: both knees pull in to the chest and the hands come in near the shins; he spins through the rest of the turn, compact (about 270 degrees).
- Tick 72, the flip completes: upright again, the legs open down under him, the arms open out.
- Tick 80: recovered, balanced, close to the fall pose; from here the player can act.
- Tick 96: the fall pose, matching tick 0.

Flow. The hips lead the turn; the chest trails 1-3 ticks, the head and arms trail more, and the arms keep moving while the body spins (moving holds, never a frozen pose). The pointed foot leads the leg on the way up. The fingers loosen and curl a little with the arm swings. After the kick, the recovery is plain: the flip completes, the body rebalances and the arms take the shortest calm path back to the fall pose. No gesture, no flourish in the ending.
